2027-01-05.title: 5 January · Tuesday after the Epiphany
readings: Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
He had compassion for them; the loaves are multiplied
2027-01-05.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-05.verse: In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
theo: St John writes the three words that sum up the Bible: “God is love.” He does not say only that God loves, but that love is what God is: the eternal exchange of Father, Son and Spirit. And he shows where we see it: “not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son.” Love begins with God, not with us. Our love is always an answer.

Mark shows that love in action. Jesus sees a great crowd, and “he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd.” First he feeds them with his word; then, when evening comes, he feeds them with bread. The disciples want to send the people away; Jesus says, “You give them something to eat.” Five loaves and two fish, blessed, broken and given, become enough for five thousand, with twelve baskets left over. The words he uses, took, blessed, broke, gave, are the words of the Last Supper. Every Eucharist is this compassion of the Shepherd.
outline: Ask: when did someone notice your need before you asked?
live: Give a meal or groceries to a family in need this week.
Thank God for one way he loved you first.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you had compassion on the hungry crowd. Take my five loaves and two fish, bless them and use them for others, and teach me to love as you have loved me. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the priest takes the bread, blesses, breaks and gives. The miracle of the loaves continues: the Shepherd feeds his flock with himself.

quick: God is love, and he loved us first.
Jesus has compassion on the crowd like a shepherd.
He multiplies our little when we give it to him.
2027-01-05.action: Give a meal or groceries to a family in need this week.
2027-01-05.question: What are my five loaves that Jesus is asking me to give?

family.explain: Many hungry people followed Jesus. A few loaves and fish were all they had. Jesus blessed them, and everyone ate until they were full!
family.intention: We pray for children who go to bed hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone this week?”

illus: In a parish in Palakkad, a widow began cooking one extra packet of rice each day for a sick neighbour. Others heard and joined her. A year later the parish kitchen was feeding forty people daily. It began with one packet given with love.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you had compassion on the crowd and fed them with your word and with bread. Feed us now, and make us generous. Amen.
share: God is love (1 John 4:8). How have I experienced God's love this week?
He had compassion for them (Mark 6:34). Whom do I find it hard to have compassion for?
You give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). What can I give?
interc: For the Church, that she may show the compassion of the Good Shepherd.
For the hungry and the poor of our land.
For farmers and all who produce our food.
For those who feel like sheep without a shepherd.
For our group, that we may share what we have.
pm.close: Lord God, you are love, and you loved us first. Make us share our bread and our lives, as your Son shared himself with us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St John today writes the most famous sentence of his letter: God is love (1 John 4:8). Not only does God love; love is what God is, from all eternity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

And John tells us where we can see this love: in this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son (1 John 4:10). Our love is always a reply. Before we ever prayed, God loved us.

In the Gospel Jesus sees a great crowd and has compassion for them, because they are like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34). He first teaches them, feeding their minds and hearts. Then evening comes and they are hungry.

The disciples say: send them away. Jesus says: you give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus takes them, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks and gives. Five thousand eat and twelve baskets are left over. Our little in his hands becomes enough.
These are the words of the Last Supper and of every Mass: took, blessed, broke, gave. Let us bring our five loaves today, our time, our money, our talents, and let him multiply them for others. Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples had only five loaves and two fish, and Jesus fed thousands of people! When you share, Jesus can do great things with your little gift.

intro: The compassion of the Shepherd who feeds his flock.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
points.apply: Notice one person in need today before they ask.

points.h: You give them something to eat
sub: The disciples want to send them away.
q: But his servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred people?” So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give it to them to eat?”
points.apply: Give food to a family in need this week.

q: the LORD appeared to him from far away. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, for God is love.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for three signs of his love.

concl: The miracle of the loaves continues at every altar.
